gaps.s: A drawing you make while visiting an original painting is a ___ source.
A book about an artist is a ___ source.
A careful copy of part of an artist's work is called a ___ study.
AO1 asks for critical ___ of sources.
The time, place and culture in which a work was made is its ___.
Using an artist's technique on your own subject is a study in the ___ of that artist.
Each component is worth ___ marks in total.
Research should link to your own ___, meaning what you want to achieve.

short.q: Explain why a page of copied biography gains few AO1 marks.
short.model: It shows no personal analysis and no link to the student's own ideas, so it shows limited critical understanding.

short.q: Name one artist and describe a practical study you could make from their work.
short.model: Kara Walker: cut a layered black paper silhouette scene about my theme and photograph it against light to test contrast.

short.q: Why does Pearson expect first-hand experience of original work?
short.model: Seeing the original shows scale, surface and colour that reproductions lose, so your research is genuinely your own.

short.q: Write one sentence of critical judgement about an artist's technique you tested.
short.model: The blurred edges gave a memory-like effect, but they hid the faces, so I will blur only the background next time.

short.q: Give two things to include besides an image on a contextual study page.
short.model: An analysis of how the work is made and a practical response, plus a note on how it will influence my own work.
